distribution: Didong (700 m a.s.l.) and Beibeng (800 m a.s.l.), Medog, Xizang; abroad it is found in Sadiya, Assam, India.
soldier: Head yellow to dark brown, the antennae pale yellow or tinged with brown, the mandibles dark brown, the thorax, legs and abdomen greyish yellow. Head oval and flat, the anterior part contracted and inclined, longer than wide, widest at the middle of the head, the posterior margin circular. Labrum lingulate, longer than wide, widest at the base, with about seven bristles regularly arranged on each side. Mandibles slender and sabre-like, the apices slightly curved; the left marginal tooth near one-quarter from the apex, with another small tooth often near the base; the right mandible has an undeveloped tooth about one-quarter from the apex and also a small tooth at the base. Antennae usually with 16 segments, segment 1 cylindrical and the longest, segment 4 the shortest. Postmentum longer than wide, with fine setae anteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, less wide than the head, the anterior margin projecting forwards like a leaf and with a median notch, the posterior margin contracting at the sides and concave at the middle.
taxonomy_note: The original work records this as Odontotermes assamensis; it is now merged, as a synonym, into O. obesus.
